definition: How much magnetic field passes through an area, $\Phi = BA\cos\theta$ with $\theta$ measured between the field and the normal to the area, in webers ($\pu{1 Wb} = \pu{1 T m2}$).
An emf produced in a conductor when the magnetic flux linked with it changes; Faraday's law gives its size and Lenz's law its direction.
The size of an induced emf equals the rate of change of flux linkage, $\varepsilon = N\frac{\Delta\Phi}{\Delta t}$, where $N$ is the number of turns.
An induced emf acts in the direction that makes its current oppose the change in flux causing it, a consequence of conservation of energy.
The emf $\varepsilon = BvL$ induced between the ends of a straight conductor of length $L$ moving at speed $v$ at right angles to a uniform magnetic field $B$.
